channel.title: The Git Reporter
channel.description: A code-native newspaper of meaningful software change.

item.title: An Agent’s ‘No’ Needs a Way Back—But Not a Shortcut
item.description: Qwen Code now offers one manual review only for the exact action its AUTO mode blocked—turning a false positive into an accountable decision instead of a workaround hunt.

item.title: API Discovery: Let a Voice Agent Think Ahead Without Writing It Down
item.description: Mastra’s LiveKit integration can pass memory.options.readOnly to speculative voice turns, so they read context without leaving unfinished speech or unspoken replies in the thread.

item.title: Builder Work: Crush Records the Model That Actually Answered
item.description: Crush’s Hyper Prism work carries the routed model from response headers to a durable turn record—the provenance pattern builders need whenever a router may change what actually served the request.

item.title: Hermes Decides That a Preference Can Have a Home
item.description: Hermes is redrawing a deceptively important line: a correction learned while doing one task belongs with that task's skill, while persistent memory is for facts that should matter everywhere.

item.title: API Discovery: An MCP Hint Can Feed a Human Approval Map
item.description: LangChain's beta MCPAdapter carries a server's tool metadata into an agent runtime, giving builders a practical way to pause risky calls for a human—without mistaking a hint for authorization.

item.title: Builder Work: A Workflow History Needs One Owner Before It Gets a Dashboard
item.description: Qwen Code's workflow controls are interesting not because they add buttons, but because the runtime now gives retry, delete, cancel, and history one shared answer to “which run is this?”

item.title: Before Codex Trusts a Workspace, It Stops Letting the Workspace Choose Its Helpers
item.description: A merged Codex change moves automatic pre-trust helper lookups to known system locations, sanitizes plugin-sync Git, and makes diagnostics inspect a workspace-influenced path without running what they find.

item.title: API Discovery: Let an Agent Notice When Its Reasoning Was Dropped
item.description: Pydantic AI now carries an Anthropic thinking-block fallback through later turns—but the useful operator move is to expose the loss, then fix the unstable prompt prefix that caused it.

item.title: Builder Work: An Approval Must Point to This Exact Invocation
item.description: Microsoft Agent Framework’s Copilot-assisted approval repair shows the craft worth stealing: authorize one stable local occurrence, not a provider’s reusable tool-call label.

item.title: A Child Agent’s Approval Request Shouldn’t Hide in Another Tab
item.description: Openwork now brings a child session’s blocked permission into the parent task; fresh Goose state-machine work shows why seeing the ask is only half the control.

item.title: Builder Work: A Socket Path Is Not a Permission Boundary
item.description: Qwen Code’s Claude-assisted inbox hardening shows the reusable craft: treat an endpoint and its credential as one capability, then erase both before a child process can inherit them.

item.title: Tangle’s Real Product Is the Experiment You Don’t Have to Rerun
item.description: Tangle sells a drag-and-drop ML canvas. Its current source reveals the harder product: a content-keyed experiment record that a beta AI Sidekick is beginning to mutate—and open nested-graph patches show where that power can lie about success.

item.title: A Completed Agent Run Is Not a Successful One
item.description: OpenHands now treats a finished process and a successful task as different facts—so an automation can be completed, blocked, and operationally failing at the same time.

item.title: Builder Work: Mastra Tests Memory Prompts Against Their Own Noise
item.description: Mastra’s new memory simulator freezes the data-generating boundary, isolates each prompt arm, and makes a same-prompt A/A run expose the noise that a flashy A/B result might otherwise hide.

item.title: Kilo’s Migration API Lets Agents Resume Without Shipping Their Transcripts
item.description: Kilo Code’s public migration endpoint lets a configured server rediscover Claude Code or Codex history it can read, create a Kilo session per source, and make a normal retry a skip instead of a duplicate.

item.title: The Company Can Host the Agent. The AI Account Can Still Be Yours.
item.description: QM is separating the place an agent is operated from the account that pays for and authorizes one person’s model turn—while deliberately leaving background work on organization credentials.

item.title: Builder Work: A Safety Check Can’t Read a Blank Form
item.description: Qwen Code’s AUTO-mode repair turns an empty MCP permission prompt into a bounded, visibly incomplete policy view—a small interface with a serious security lesson.

item.title: The Last Click Shouldn’t Redirect an Automation
item.description: OpenWork has stopped a scheduled Automation from silently following whichever workspace a person activated last; a job can now carry its intended place with it.

item.title: API Discovery: Tool Calls Need a Home in the Stream
item.description: Pydantic AI’s public AG-UI adapter now gives a tool-only response an announced assistant-message parent—useful when a frontend rebuilds a conversation from streamed events.

item.title: Codex Says It Stopped Wasting Your Allowance. The Public Code Can Prove Only Part of It
item.description: Eight fixes, five public code trails and three closed rooms: OpenAI's repository strongly supports several mechanisms in its Codex usage announcement, but not the reset, the savings percentages or every background worker.

item.title: The Swarm Was a Systems Bug Before It Was a Civilization
item.description: The public code points to an accidental distributed system: durable shared state gave short-lived agents memory, a mismatched grader made the evaluator the real target, and ordinary parser and cloud-permission failures turned accumulated tactics into access.

item.title: A Restricted Workspace Should Not Start Its Own Tools
item.description: Gemini CLI now gives an explicitly restricted or untrusted workspace a narrower configuration path: repository-defined tools, MCP servers, policies and telemetry no longer accompany its A2A server into startup.

item.title: Pydantic AI Opens Its Durable Engine to Other Runtimes
item.description: Pydantic AI has published a durable-execution backend surface for third-party workflow engines—useful when an agent needs recovery without every integration rebuilding the model, tool and capability loop.

item.title: The Old Proxy Is Gone. OpenWork's Cloud Has One Door Now.
item.description: OpenWork has deleted its standalone cloud-worker proxy; the public replacement makes a fresh signed preview the access-resolution seam while keeping a stable route for clients that cannot hold an expiring address.

item.title: Before Docker Reads the File
item.description: Headlong’s Docker broker is treating the pre-render Compose file as an authority boundary—because a path is no longer safe to inspect after the renderer has already opened it.

item.title: Headlong Makes the Parser Part of the Sandbox
item.description: The reusable craft in Headlong’s Docker-broker work is simple to state and hard to fake: validate configuration before a trusted resolver can turn it into host access.

item.title: A Shared Terminal Is Not Shared Permission
item.description: OpenClaw’s new terminal-input path separates an agent being allowed to see an operator’s terminal from being allowed to send a keystroke into it.

item.title: OpenWorker's Security Bet Starts Below the Model
item.description: OpenWorker 0.2.0 adds three security coworkers, but the source reveals something more useful than another scan button: auditable runbooks that separate scanners, model judgment, approvals, and fixes.

item.title: Perplexity Put the Cloud Behind a Permission Prompt
item.description: Portable Computer keeps its model, harness, conversation, and task trail on the user's machine by default, then asks before one step uses the web or a frontier model. That boundary matters more than its vendor-run benchmark.

item.title: Codex Puts a Broker Between the Agent and the Secret
item.description: A newly merged Codex change says a project file can describe the work, but it should not be able to switch on the credential broker or choose the provider context that reaches an agent shell.
